title: Generate Binary Strings Without Adjacent Zeros
description:
You are given a positive integer n . 
 
 A binary string x is valid if all substrings of x of length 2 contain at least one "1" . 
 
 Return all valid strings with length n , in any order. 

 Example 1: 

 Input: n = 3 
 
 Output: ["010","011","101","110","111"] 
 
 Explanation: 
 
 The valid strings of length 3 are: "010" , "011" , "101" , "110" , and "111" . 

 Example 2: 

 Input: n = 1 
 
 Output: ["0","1"] 
 
 Explanation: 
 
 The valid strings of length 1 are: "0" and "1" . 

 Constraints: 

 1 <= n <= 18
code: class Solution {void dfs(int n,string&s,vector<string>&out){if((int)s.size()==n){out.push_back(s);return;}s+='1';dfs(n,s,out);s.pop_back();if(s.empty()||s.back()=='1'){s+='0';dfs(n,s,out);s.pop_back();}}public:vector<string> validStrings(int n){vector<string>r;string s;dfs(n,s,r);return r;}};
